results.title: iOS 17 review: Notable new features and streamlined touches
results.content: Lots of improvements for iPhone users with iPhone-using friends. iOS 17 brings some substantial new features and a lot of upgrades that streamline how you use your iPhone, especially when connecting with other iPhone users. While the lock screen customizations introduced in iOS 16 formed the big visual change last year, Apple has now applied a similar makeover to your phone calls and contact lists. And at a time when there is no shortage of video call apps and services, it's trying to make FaceTime even more compelling. When I previewed the developer build a month or so ago, I focused on messages and FaceTime, both of which got a lot of attention in this update. After a little more time with the finished product, iOS 17 feels like a big quality-of-life upgrade for iPhone users. Without a big tentpole feature, it's harder to pinpoint why it's so much better — but I'll try.

results.title: iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max review: An impactful redesign
results.content: # iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max review: An impactful redesign. An iPhone 17 Pro with its screen facing out and an iPhone 17 Pro Max with its rear facing out. The reason I've been playing so much *Snake Clash* is because I've noticed in my year with an iPhone 16 Pro that countless hours with games like this cause the device to burn up in my hands. I spent a lot of time on the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max trying to get them to run hot, because one of the most interesting additions this year is a vapor chamber. For this review, I focused on the performance, thermal management, camera capabilities and battery life of the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. I am bundling them together because aside from screen size, battery capacity and price, the two are functionally identical. When I first picked up the iPhone 17 Pro at Apple Park, I found it refreshingly different from the iPhone 16 Pro I'd been using for a year (and also the iPhone 15 Pro before that).

results.title: The iPhone 17 boasts a larger display with ProMotion support and a 120Hz refresh rate
results.content: # The iPhone 17 boasts a larger display with ProMotion support and a 120Hz refresh rate. At 6.3 inches, it's larger than the iPhone 16's 6.1-inch screen. Not only is the iPhone 17 screen larger than the one on its predecessor, it boasts a Super Retina XDR display with ProMotion, meaning it has an adaptive refresh rate of up to 120Hz for smoother scrolling (you can perhaps thank my colleague Igor Bonifacic for willing that into existence). No prizes for guessing that there's an upgraded processor in the iPhone 17. There's also a 48MP ultrawide sensor — Apple says this can capture up to four times the resolution of the previous-gen camera. As for the front-facing camera, it has a much larger sensor than on previous models, according to Apple. On the battery front, Apple says the iPhone 17 will deliver up to 30 hours of continuous video playback on a single charge, which is eight hours more than on the iPhone 16.
